To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the spiral curriculum for general practice is a feasible concept, but that it requires a high degree of commitment to the concept and to the development of the spiral curriculum.
the spiral curriculum is a concept that can be used to describe the undergraduate-postgraduate interface in general practice.
the spiral curriculum is a concept that can be used in undergraduate-postgraduate co-operational learning.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development and evaluation of a'spiral' undergraduate curriculum, in which core competencies are taught at increasing levels of complexity, and the use of the spiral curriculum in undergraduate-postgraduate co-operative learning.
the development of an integrated curriculum in which general practice plays a central part.
the development of an undergraduate curriculum that will produce doctors with the skills and attitudes to work in primary health care teams.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the undergraduate curriculum should be a spiral one that is continuous with the postgraduate curriculum, but with the content and delivery being determined by the needs of both.
the undergraduate-postgraduate collaboration is an ideal way of developing a spiral curriculum for general practice.
the undergraduate-postgraduate collaboration is essential to achieve a successful spiral curriculum for general practice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the development of the spiral curriculum should be seen as an ideal area for co-operation between undergraduate and postgraduate departments.
the undergraduate curriculum should be a spiral curriculum in which topics may re-visited at different levels of complexity during the learning.
undergraduate departments need to be more proactive in developing their own curriculum and the assessment of it, and in working with the postgraduate community.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the undergraduate curriculum is not a separate entity but is a continuum of learning, which can be developed in collaboration with postgraduate colleagues to the benefit of all concerned.
we need to be more explicit and more systematic in our efforts to integrate the curriculum and the learning experience.
the undergraduate curriculum is not a static entity, and that it should be constantly evolving.
